cells.tense: You are standing at the far side of something, and you can name what it held.
cells.ask: Ask someone you trust how they saw one recent ending. Practice on their view first — the part you can't see yet may be easier to spot from outside.
cells.core:
Nearly everything gets clearer for you at the end of a stretch, and you're at the end of one now. You can turn and look at what it held without flinching, and you say it plainly. The feeling is full rather than finished, which is why it holds up when you talk about it. Not everything in it is resolved. That's part of what you see.

This kind of seeing feeds what comes next, the way a full meal feeds the body. It's available to you. If you want to spend it, hand it to someone else — speak what you notice in their situation and let them keep what's right. Connection through what you've seen feeds both of you.
cells.sheetLine: You can see the whole of it and still not be finished.
cells.verb: seeing the whole span of what this feeling holds, and calling it by name
cells.place: where the next step shows up before the whole road does

cells.tense: You are braced against a moment you can't write into the open — finishing before it has actually finished.
cells.ask: Pick one plan you've been carrying. Say plainly why it still stands, without checking its weakness again. Ten minutes.
cells.core:
You keep trying to reach the far end of a feeling before it's actually arrived — wanting the whole thing finished, closed, understood, so you can say you're through it. But you're reading a map of the end instead of standing in the middle. The push is crowded with what you'd like to be true.

That bracing runs ahead of where you actually are. A small clear thing to do next is what's needed — one direction, chosen because it is right, not because you're forcing the ending. Let what's here be enough for one step instead of demanding it be finished.
cells.sheetLine: You can't finish a season before it has run.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that has already closed behind you, still waiting to be let through.
cells.ask: Say yes to one small thing you'd normally assess first — a walk, a call, a question. Nothing to prepare.
cells.core:
Going well, this looks like walking into a room with nothing decided. You read what's in front of you as it comes, one thing at a time, and you don't need the ending to make sense before you start. That kind of openness isn't lost, just not being used.

When something arrives now, it doesn't quite land — the version you could say feels finished already, as if the rest happened without you. Taking in the whole shape of something hasn't gone anywhere. It just isn't being turned toward anything fresh.

What wakes it isn't more looking. It's starting one new thing before you're ready — a spark that hasn't found its direction yet, and isn't supposed to. Reach toward that, and the whole-shape seeing comes back with it. Learn one person's situation, agree to one easy outing, ask a question you can't answer yet — nothing where the ending matters.
cells.sheetLine: You're still looking back at a door you already walked through.

cells.tense: You have already seen the whole thing, and you are calling that nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Name one thing you saw before you talked yourself out of it, and go with it this time — no second look.
cells.core:
A knowing shows up about how something turned out — not guessed, not hoped — and it gets filed as nothing much. The read from the room carries more weight than the one that arrived on its own. But the perceiving has been going the whole time. The mind was holding the truth and weighing it before saying it. That's not a mood. It's a faculty.

The writing isn't acknowledged, not absent. When you say what already showed up before you check it against the room, the whole picture comes back into your own hands. Try it once, and let the recognition belong to the one it belongs to — a small decision made on your own read, kept.
cells.sheetLine: You saw it before you knew you saw it.
